title: ObjectiveContract
description: Goal-completion governance contract. Required when Plan.goal_type ∈ {parity, new_feature, migration, incident}. Describes the user-facing outcome the plan must satisfy, separate from the mechanical artifacts produced (which features.json describes). The plan-level validator enforces that goal_type here matches Plan.goal_type when both are present.

goal_type.description: Must match Plan.goal_type at the parent plan when both are present. Expanded from the original four (parity/new_feature/migration/incident) to the full Plan goal_type set so the lite universal contract (delivers-only, no user_journeys) can attach to infra/refactor/mechanical plans at schema_version >= 1.1.

source_of_truth.description: Reference to the canonical source (PRD path, source-platform name for parity, incident report URL, prior plan id, etc.). Does NOT need to be a live repo URL; static curated references are valid.

user_journeys.description: User-facing flows the goal must satisfy end-to-end. The auditor walks these against the proposed features at pre-impl time and against shipped patches at post-impl time.

description.description: What the user does, end-to-end. Substantive enough that the auditor can reason about coverage gaps.

states.description: States the journey transitions through (e.g., 'empty', 'loading', 'error', 'success'). Optional.

acceptance_signals.description: What the auditor should look for to confirm journey coverage. Optional but recommended.

required_evidence.description: Evidence the post-impl audit (Plan F2) must produce (screenshots, logs, journey walks). Optional at pre-impl time; load-bearing at post-impl.

non_goals.description: Explicit out-of-scope items. Prevents scope-creep findings during sufficiency audit and integration audit.

completion_test.description: One-sentence prose answering 'how do we know this is done?'. The completion test is the operator's stake in the ground; the auditor checks the proposed features against it.

delivers.description: Audience-first outcome statements: what becomes true, for whom, what kind of capability, and which features prove it. Required (non-empty) when the plan declares schema_version >= 1.1; advisory below that (the plan-level validator warns inline rather than failing). Complements user_journeys, which stays optional — a substrate/infra plan may carry delivers[] with no journeys.

audience.description: Who can now safely do something they couldn't before.

kind.description: The kind of capability delivered. 'No new screen' is not 'no capability' — durability/recoverability/enforceable controls are reliability/safety/infrastructure outcomes.

capability.description: Plain-language statement of what this audience can now do. No feature IDs — those belong in proof_refs.

proof.description: Optional cheap first-principle proof for THIS slice: the measurement that would show the capability is true, and how it is taken. Distinct from proof_refs — proof_refs point at features that were built, proof names what you would measure to falsify delivery. Optional at the schema layer by design: absence is valid here, and the lock/close scorer (plan 2026-08-13-001 F002) decides whether a missing proof is inferred, an accepted gap, or a close-time failure. If defining the proof is harder than the work, the proof is wrong.

metric.description: The cheap measurement that would show this capability is true — a threshold, a count, an observable state change. Substantive enough that a reader can tell whether it was met (hence the 10-character floor); not a KPI programme.

method.description: How the metric is taken. 'walk' — a human or agent walks the path end-to-end. 'request' — a single call against a running surface. 'named_test' — an existing or new test identified by name. 'probe' — a one-off script or query run against real state. Closed set on purpose: anything requiring a warehouse, a dashboard, or a quarter of data is not a cheap proof and does not belong in a lock.

surface.description: Optional — where the proof is taken. Mirrors the plan-level `surfaces` enum in plan.schema.json; the two are kept in lockstep and asserted identical by scripts/test_objective_contract_proof.py. Singular because a cheap proof is taken in one place.

proof_refs.description: Typed references to the evidence that proves the capability. Reference features rather than restating their verdicts, so proof can't drift from features.json.

type.description: Ref kind. v0 supports 'feature'; extend this enum (not a path grammar like '002/F014') for future ref kinds.

id.description: Feature id (F001–F999) in the target plan's features.json.

plan.description: Optional cross-plan target id. Absent = same plan as this contract.

inherits.description: Optional plan id this contract deltas from. Set it on a child or fix plan whose outcome is the parent's outcome: the parent names what becomes true, and this contract's delivers[] carries only the delta — one slice, not a restatement of the parent's full set. delivers[] stays required and non-empty at plan schema_version >= 1.1 (a delta IS a delivers[]); what inherits licenses is omitting the FULL set, not omitting the block. Resolution of the pointer (does the parent exist, does it carry an outcome) is a lock-time concern, not a schema one — see plan 2026-08-13-001 F002.
inherits.$comment: Same plan-id grammar as delivers[].proof_refs[].plan; keep the two patterns in lockstep.

cluster_overrides.description: Optional override notes for the Goal Governance V1 §6.3 cluster coherence rule. Free-form for v1; future versions may structure this. Only set when the default rule (subsystem_and_journey intersection) doesn't fit the plan's gap-clustering pattern.
